setup.command:
cd MFQ && uv run python -c "
import json, os, pathlib
import torch
from safetensors.torch import save_file
# create tiny hf model
out='/tmp/tiny_hf'
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
config={
  'model_type':'qwen3',
  'hidden_size':128,
  'num_hidden_layers':2,
  'num_attention_heads':4,
  'num_key_value_heads':4,
  'intermediate_size':256,
  'vocab_size':32000,
  'max_position_embeddings':512,
  'hidden_act':'silu',
  'rms_norm_eps':1e-05
}
open(os.path.join(out,'config.json'),'w').write(json.dumps(config))
# create dummy weights matching qwen3?
# Look at expected keys: model.embed_tokens, model.layers.0 etc
sd={}
def rand(shape): return torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.float16)
sd['model.embed_tokens.weight']=rand((32000,128))
for i in range(2):
    p=f'model.layers.{i}'
    sd[f'{p}.self_attn.q_proj.weight']=rand((128,128))
    sd[f'{p}.self_attn.k_proj.weight']=rand((128,128))
    sd[f'{p}.self_attn.v_proj.weight']=rand((128,128))
    sd[f'{p}.self_attn.o_proj.weight']=rand((128,128))
    sd[f'{p}.mlp.gate_proj.weight']=rand((256,128))
    sd[f'{p}.mlp.up_proj.weight']=rand((256,128))
    sd[f'{p}.mlp.down_proj.weight']=rand((128,256))
    sd[f'{p}.input_layernorm.weight']=rand((128,))
    sd[f'{p}.post_attention_layernorm.weight']=rand((128,))
sd['model.norm.weight']=rand((128,))
sd['lm_head.weight']=rand((32000,128))
save_file(sd, os.path.join(out,'model.safetensors'))
print('done', os.listdir(out))
" 2>&1

pitfalls.readme_said: uv sync + uv run mfq build --backend auto works on any host
pitfalls.actually_needed: build requires CUDA toolkit nvcc/CMake or Apple Silicon Metal; on plain Linux x86 without accelerator it fails with 'no supported inference accelerator was detected'

pitfalls.readme_said: uv run mfq serve starts server
pitfalls.actually_needed: serve also auto-detects backend and fails with same BuildError when no accelerator present, so F3 cannot be tested in this sandbox
quantize --backend cpu works with torch+extra train deps, verified with tiny synthetic Qwen3 checkpoint; README example uses --backend auto which would require accelerator

judge.observed: All three screenshots show version 0.1.0, dry-run quantize plan with mfq_quantize event, and full quantize finishing with status ok.

findings.summary: zip: Critical Parser Differential & Security Control Bypass via Dual-Header Inconsistencies (Zip Cloaking) Leading to Arbitrary File Overwrite & RCE
ZipStreamReader::extract() and ZipArchive::extract() apply Unix permissions through symlinks without confining the target
DOMPurify SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES bypass: split template expressions survive in attached shadow root content on DOM output modes
Peer minimum ACK delay can panic quinn-proto when ACK_FREQUENCY transmission is enabled
Stream reassembly memory-exhaustion guard in quinn-proto can be bypassed
zip: legacy Shrink/Reduce/Implode decoder: denial of service from attacker-controlled ZIP64 uncompressed size
zip: Arbitrary file write outside the extraction directory, because ZipArchive::extract validates symlink targets lexically.
zip: Unbounded Symlink-Target Handling Can Abort Or Exhaust Memory During Extraction
Insecure Preservation of SUID/SGID Bits during ZIP Extraction Leading to Potential Privilege Escalation
DOMPurify IN_PLACE: hook that removes a parent or sibling leaves the detached subtree's event handlers armed (incomplete fix for GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p)
